page: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine powered by AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated physical vCPUs driven by an ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-N1 processor operating at 2.5 GHz, with single-threaded physical core execution and no simultaneous multithreading. System memory totals 16.0 GB, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory distribution of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include integrated local disk storage, necessitating remote network-attached volumes, and it includes no discrete GPU accelerators. Networking is defined by a baseline bandwidth rating of 1 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark measurements characterize the m6g.xlarge as having stable memory throughput paired with modest multi-core compute capability. Memory bandwidth testing shows 71.14 GB/sec for uncached large block reads and 34.79 GB/sec for uncached writes, placing memory bandwidth in the middle tiers. In processing benchmarks, the instance yields a stress-ng single-core score of 1489.98 and a multi-core score of 5934.04. Synthetic compute assessments demonstrate lower throughput against higher-frequency architectures, posting 954.0 in Geekbench single-core, 3166.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and an overall PassMark CPU score of 2687.62.

The absence of hyperthreading overhead provides consistent per-core execution, which benefits predictability on ARM-native applications. With its balanced resource profile and lack of local NVMe storage, the m6g.xlarge is designed for balanced enterprise workloads. It operates effectively as a host for distributed microservices, Redis caching instances, lightweight application backends, web servers, and continuous integration environments targeting ARM architectures.
description: Amazon Web Services m6g.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by an ARMv8 AWS Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. The configuration provides 4 dedicated vCPUs with 1 thread per physical core, paired with 16.0 GB of RAM to deliver a 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio. It includes no local storage volumes, no GPU hardware, and a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps. Benchmark evaluations reflect consistent memory performance, achieving 71.14 GB/sec on uncached reads, alongside moderate multi-core processing with a Geekbench multi-core rating of 3166.0 and PassMark CPU score of 2687.62. The instance delivers predictable ARM-based resource allocation without thread contention, making it suitable for web application hosting, Redis caching nodes, backend microservices, and general developer staging environments.
